text: The two operations of this capability are POST and GET /notices/{noticeId}/responses under the base /api/recovery/comms/v1, with the Idempotency-Key header on the POST and its stored answer, and the statuses 401, 403, 404, 409, 422 and 503.
why: The legacy story copies only the two notice operations and the TSD P6 endpoint inventory holds no response operation, so the surface has to be fixed by this realignment; the base and the naming are fixed by DP-13 and DP-14.
read: Legacy RWB-E4-036 endpoints and permission checks; FSD P6 A2.15; TSD P6 v2 T-A.1; Template and Rules v1 R4 naming, R7.3 fill order and DP-13
confirm: The rwb-comms tech lead confirms the two paths and the statuses when the rwb-comms OpenAPI document is baselined, and the gateway-bff owner confirms the route.
impact: The channel and the case record panel call the two paths; a response operation published elsewhere later would need an alias and a version note.

text: The customer response is stored in a new table notice_response of rwb_comms with the columns id, notice_id, case_id, response_code, channel, responded_at, decision_record_id and the standard columns of TSD P6 T3.0; the names, the types and the required flags are fixed in RWB-P6-E4036-CON and their DF field ids stand as the placeholder.
why: No source declares a response table for this module and the acceptance cannot be stored without one, so the row is declared and its unnamed parts carry the placeholder rather than a guessed name.
read: TSD P6 v2 T3.1 and T3.0; Legacy RWB-E4-036 data table; Template and Rules v1 R9 placeholder rule and DP-01
confirm: The data steward and the rwb-comms tech lead confirm the table, its columns and its field ids when the Logical Data Model and Data Dictionary next publish.
impact: One new table and one Flyway step in rwb_comms; a renamed column later is an additive change within major version 1 or a new major version of the contract.

text: The capability area of the two response operations is Litigation, with right C on the POST and right R on the GET and scope applied, and the customer is identified at the edge by the gateway-bff session; the role lists stay rwb-access data.
why: The legacy permission check names Litigation C and Litigation R, the TSD P6 RBAC matrix holds no customer role and no right for a self-service answer, and the legacy copy is the only statement of a right that exists for this key.
read: Legacy RWB-E4-036 permission checks; TSD P6 v2 T6.1 and T6.2; Template and Rules v1 DP-19 and R7.3 fill order
confirm: The solution architect and the rwb-access owner confirm the capability area, the right and the customer identity at the edge when the edge contract is baselined.
impact: If a new capability area is created for self-service, the two operations change area and the role lists are re-seeded in rwb-access; no code change beyond the declaration.

text: The offer of the case, the acceptance recorded on the case and the contact point with its consent are consumed and faked on the owners contracts, and the events TreatmentApproved and CaseStateChanged are consumed with the inbox dedupe; no C dependency is declared and the two unnamed paths stand as the placeholder.
why: The plan names no contract story of S2, P3 or P1 for this key and the C list is empty, while the capability cannot run without those three facts and the two events; the checks forbid an I dependency outside an ITG story.
read: Ownership Map v1; Architecture v5 slides 17 and 42; Template and Rules v1 R5.4 dependency classes, DP-05 and DP-11
confirm: The solution architect confirms the three consumed rows and the two events, and adds the C rows when the owner contract stories are planned.
impact: Every test runs against the fakes until the owners publish; a later contract of an owner is an additive adoption and no rebuild of this capability.

text: The decision element of a response carries the case, the notice, the party, the response code, the channel, the responded at, the decision code, the rule id and the rule version, with the rule ids R-RES-16 and R-RES-17 and every other value read as reference data; the response-code list and the decision code stand as the placeholder.
why: Legacy AC1 requires the rule version and the routing table gives only the two events, so the element can be fixed while its values stay data; inventing a code or a member list would break the no-business-value guardrail.
read: Legacy RWB-E4-036 AC1; Business Rules and Routing Logic v4 rows R-RES-16 and R-RES-17; Template and Rules v1 DP-03 and R7.2 s17
confirm: The business analyst and the rwb-decision owner confirm the decision code, the response-code list and the rule version source when the reference data is published.
impact: A response is recorded with a code that the reference data supplies; a missing code refuses the write closed and no decision is recorded.

text: This service serves the two response operations and no screen of its own, a notice carries one response, and the refusal texts beyond the five legacy messages and the mapping of the HOME.SCB channel to a LOV-CHANNEL code stand as the placeholder.
why: The only P6 screen is the template screen, no source names a response surface, no source states a second distinct response and no source gives the texts of the remaining refusals or the channel mapping.
read: FSD P6 v3 Screens and A2.15; Legacy RWB-E4-036 screen and validation table; TSD P6 v2 T3.2; Template and Rules v1 R7.2 s17
confirm: The business analyst and the owner of the message list confirm the surface, the one-response rule, the refusal texts and the channel mapping.
impact: The officer reads the answers on the case record panel through the composite route; a second distinct response is refused and the first stands.

text: The dispute of rwb-comms is served by POST /notices/{noticeId}/disputes and GET /notices/{noticeId}/disputes under /api/recovery/comms/v1, with the DisputeRequest and Dispute shapes and a new table notice_dispute in rwb_comms whose element names, physical types, required flags, state list and DF field ids are fixed at the contract baseline and marked where no source names them.
why: No source names a dispute operation, a request, an answer or a table for rwb-comms, and FEAT-COM-04 asks for the outcome only, so the surface that carries it has to be fixed before RWB-P6-E4038-APP can build on Day 1.
read: FSD P6 A2.17; TSD P6 v2 T3.1 and T-A.1; Architecture v5 slide 17; legacy RWB-E4-038
confirm: Tech lead of rwb-comms and the data steward at the contract baseline review
impact: The paths, the two schemas and the new table are frozen for the app story; a change after sign-off needs a new major version of the document.

text: X1 is raised on the rwb-deviation contract (the Ownership Map row POST /cases/{caseId}/deviations) with the case, the notice, the dispute, the channel and the reason code, and the answer carries the deviation identifier that the dispute stores as its owner reference; the call and the deviation read are consumed and faked, add no C row, and an unanswered raise leaves the dispute recorded with the stop in force, no reference, a retry and an alert.
why: R-UNI-04 and the Ownership Map put the deviation and its pause with S8, and no S8 contract story is planned for this key, so the call cannot be built against a published owner contract.
read: Business Rules and Routing Logic v4 R-UNI-04, R-RES-19, R-SET-12; Ownership Map rows owned by S8; Architecture v5 slide 41; TSD P6 v2 T5.2
confirm: Owner of rwb-deviation at the contract baseline review
impact: No contract dependency is declared; the fake and the 202 branch carry the risk until an S8 contract story exists, and the stop is never released by this service.

text: The principal of a self-service dispute is the authenticated customer of LINE OA or HOME.SCB passed by gateway-bff with the case scope, and no role code of the rights matrix is written for it; the two operations declare the capability area Documents with right C on the POST and right R on the GET, enforced at the edge, and the Complaint officer (RW-COMPLAIN) is the internal principal who records and reads a dispute.
why: The FSD names the customer as the primary actor while TSD P6 T6.1 has no customer row, so the action has no Workbench role to hold its right.
read: FSD P6 A2.17.3.3 and A2.17.2 (integration points LINE OA, HOME.SCB); TSD P6 v2 T6.1; Architecture v5 slides 13 and 20
confirm: Platform route owner and the security architect
impact: No P4 dependency and no role table are declared; object-level authorisation is the case scope the edge passes, and the rights matrix gains a customer row later.

text: The legacy rows that name SCR-33 Template approval, Litigation C and Litigation R, POST /cases/{caseId}/notices and GET /notices/{noticeId} belong to the notice and template features of this service and are not copied into the dispute stories; REQ-OCC-011 is the requirement the dispute serves, and the T8 mapping of TSD P6 to FEAT-COM-01 is a documentation defect.
why: The legacy story body is a customer self-service action while its own screen, permission and endpoint tables describe notice administration, and the higher sources place those rows in the notice feature.
read: Legacy RWB-E4-038 Screen and states, Permission checks and Endpoints; FSD P6 A2.17 and requirements served; TSD P6 v2 T6.1 and T8
confirm: Business analyst, P6, at the story review
impact: No notice or template row is copied into the dispute stories and no Litigation right is claimed for a customer action; the traceability row carries the conflict.

text: The contact stop is applied to the outbound contact of the notice through notice.hold_reason (DF-LEG-032), set from the raise and from rwb.deviation.DeviationRaised.v1 and cleared only on rwb.deviation.DeviationCleared.v1, with the consumer element of the two events declared in the contract and the dispute state list read as reference data; no source value, no payload field and no state name is written as a constant.
why: Slide 17 names the two events for the contact stop and TSD P6 holds hold_reason, but no source gives the payload, the key or the stop state, so the carrier and the projection must be fixed rather than invented per story.
read: Architecture v5 slides 17 and 42 (rows 06 and 07); TSD P6 v2 T3.1 (DF-LEG-032); Business Rules and Routing Logic v4 R-LIT-05 and R-UNI-44
confirm: Owner of rwb-deviation and the Tech lead of rwb-comms
impact: The hold is one nullable column of the notice that the dispatch path reads; the payload of the two events stays the owner's and the lift is applied from the event and from nothing else.

text: The dispute reason codes, the dispute state list, the decision code, the rule id and the refusal message ids and texts are reference data, parameters and message-list entries read with the version in force, and the refusals that no source names are carried as the placeholder of section 14 of each story.
why: BR-P6-017 forbids writing in code a value a business person may change and no source gives these values, so they cannot be fixed in the story or in the code.
read: FSD P6 A2.17.3.1 (BR-P6-017); legacy RWB-E4-038 Validation and messages; Template and Rules R7.2 s17
confirm: Configuration owner and the owner of the message list at the wave 3 readiness review
impact: A new reason code, a new state or a new message is a data row, not a release, and no refusal text is invented in the stories or the fakes.

text: The contact point, its consent state, its verification and its failed count are P1 rwb-source-data's rows in rwb_source_data and in the ACE contact views, and rwb-comms reads and writes them only on that service's contract.
why: The Ownership Map gives contact_point_ext, party_ext, account_ext and valuation_ext to P1, while the legacy story and the FSD describe the consent state as a P6 row of the recovery schema; source precedence and DP-01 put the rows with their owner and DP-05 gives the route.
read: Recovery Workbench Ownership Map v1 (contact_point_ext, party_ext owner P1); Architecture v5 Text Extract v1 slides 17 and 41; Template and Rules v1 R5.5 DP-01 and DP-05
confirm: The solution architect confirms the Ownership Map rows for the four extension tables at the baseline review of the rwb-comms contract.
impact: rwb-comms declares no contact table and no v_ace_* query; the contact value and the consent state reach it one hop from rwb-source-data, and a decision to keep them in P6 would need a new Ownership Map ruling and a rewrite of both stories.

text: The contact read and the consent and verification write of the rwb-source-data contract are consumed and faked rows, their path and element list stand as the placeholder, and no C dependency is declared for them.
why: No source names a contact or consent operation of P1 and the plan names no P1 contract story for this key, so the rows cannot be pinned today; one hop with a 2 s timeout and a fake keep the build moving.
read: Architecture v5 Text Extract v1 slide 15 (P1 IN rows); Recovery Workbench Ownership Map v1 api rows owned by P1; Template and Rules v1 R5.4
confirm: The P1 tech lead names the two operations and their element lists when the rwb-source-data contract is published.
impact: The app story builds and tests against the fake; the pinned paths and the C row are added when P1 publishes the contract, and a path change then costs one adapter update.

text: The contact repository's two operations are new on /api/recovery/comms/v1 and are declared by RWB-P6-E4039-CON, while the two legacy notice endpoints and the legacy screen SCR-33 Template approval stay with the notice and template stories.
why: The legacy endpoint and screen tables copy the notice operations and the template screen, and the TSD P6 inventory holds no contact operation; the feature still needs a surface, so it is fixed as this key's own new contract.
read: Legacy RWB-E4-039 endpoints and screen tables; TSD P6 Communications v2 T-A.1; FSD P6 Communications v3 A2.18
confirm: The rwb-comms tech lead confirms the two paths when the rwb-comms OpenAPI document is baselined.
impact: The screen and the tests call the two new operations through the gateway-bff route; no legacy notice path is reused for a contact.

text: The consent state set, the verification rule, the failed-count threshold and the decision code of a consent change are parameters and reference data read with the version in force, and their values are left to the compliance and PDPA officer.
why: No source gives a consent value, a verification rule or a failed-count threshold, and BR-P6-018 forbids a value a business person may change from being written in code.
read: Legacy RWB-E4-039 data table (contact_point_ext); FSD P6 Communications v3 A2.18.2 and A2.18.3.1; TSD P6 Communications v2 T3.2
confirm: The compliance and PDPA officer confirms the consent set, the verification rule, the failed-count threshold and the decision code before the baseline review closes.
impact: The contract carries the values as placeholders and the service reads them as data; a later confirmation changes a parameter row and no code.

text: The contact read is declared with Documents right R and the consent write with Documents right U, scope applied, and the legacy Litigation rights stay on the notice operations of the notice stories.
why: The primary role of FEAT-COM-05 holds Documents RU and Litigation R in TSD P6 T6.1 and never Litigation C, so the legacy right copied from the notice endpoints cannot authorise the repository.
read: Legacy RWB-E4-039 permission checks; TSD P6 Communications v2 T6.1; FSD P6 Communications v3 A2.18.3.3
confirm: The solution architect confirms the two rights and the scope at the baseline review, with rwb-access holding the role lists.
impact: rwb-access grants the compliance and PDPA officer the write through Documents U; a role list change stays data and no code changes.

text: rwb-comms keeps one P6 row for the contact stop keyed by the case reference the deviation events carry, with no contact value and no consent state, and the composite contact key and the eight unnamed contact_point_ext fields stay placeholders of the owner's table.
why: The two deviation events must land somewhere in this service and no source defines a projection, while the composite key and the unnamed fields belong to P1's table and cannot be guessed here.
read: Architecture v5 Text Extract v1 slide 17 (contact-stop events); FSD P6 Communications v3 A2.18.2; legacy RWB-E4-039 data table
confirm: The rwb-comms tech lead confirms the projection shape and the P1 owner confirms the composite key and the unnamed fields of its own table.
impact: The stop mark is answerable without a case or party join; a changed key or field list changes the contract placeholder and one adapter mapping.

text: The intent is registered through a consumed and faked rwb-payment operation and the consent and the contact stop are read through a consumed and faked rwb-source-data operation; neither is declared as a C dependency, and both answer from a fake from the first run of RWB-P6-E4037-APP.
why: No P8 and no P1 contract story is named for this key and no source gives either operation, and a build dependency on a story that does not exist would block a Day-1 story of wave 3.
read: Ownership Map v1 api rows of P8 and table rows of P1; Architecture v5 slide 17 rwb-payment IN and OUT and slide 41; Template and Rules v1 R5.4 dependency classes and R5.7 rule 2
confirm: The rwb-payment and rwb-source-data owners confirm the two operations and their shapes when their contracts are baselined, and the Contract dependencies rows are amended then.
impact: Both owner calls run against fakes until the owners publish; a changed owner shape is an additive contract change with a fake refresh, and no story of this key waits for it.

text: The two operations of this capability are POST and GET /notices/{noticeId}/payment-intents under the base /api/recovery/comms/v1, with the Idempotency-Key header and its stored answer on the POST and the statuses 401, 403, 404, 409, 422 and 503; the self-service screen is the customer screen on HOME.SCB and the web, whose identifier no source gives.
why: The endpoint inventory of the module holds no self-service payment operation and the legacy story copies the two notice operations, so the surface and the screen have to be fixed by this realignment; the base, the topic and the naming are fixed by DP-13 and DP-14.
read: Legacy RWB-E4-037 Endpoints and Screen and states; FSD P6 A2.16.2; TSD P6 v2 T-A.1; Template and Rules v1 R4 naming, R7.3 fill order and DP-13
confirm: The rwb-comms tech lead confirms the two paths and the statuses when the rwb-comms OpenAPI document is baselined, and the gateway-bff owner confirms the composite route and the screen identifier.
impact: The customer channel and the case record panel call the two paths; a self-service payment operation published elsewhere later would need an alias and a version note.

text: The intent is stored in a new table payment_intent of rwb_comms with the intent id, case_id, notice_id, target, channel, the owner reference, the owner state, requested_at and the standard columns of TSD P6 T3.0; the names, the types and the required flags are fixed in RWB-P6-E4037-CON, and every DF field id of the row stands as the placeholder.
why: No source declares a payment-intent entity for this module and the intent cannot be taken, stored or answered without one, so the row is declared here and its unnamed parts carry the placeholder rather than a guessed name or type.
read: TSD P6 v2 T3.1, T3.0 and T3.3; Legacy RWB-E4-037 Data table; Template and Rules v1 R9 placeholder rule and DP-01
confirm: The data steward and the rwb-comms tech lead confirm the table, its columns and its field ids when the Logical Data Model and Data Dictionary next publish, and the CON baseline is amended additively.
impact: One new table, one Flyway step and two indexes in rwb_comms; a renamed column later is an additive change within major version 1 or a new major version of the contract.

text: The eligible notice states and the target list are parameters of rwb-comms, the channels and the owner state set are reference data read with the version in force, and the decision code and the rule id come from the reference data of rwb-decision; no such value is written in code.
why: BR-P6-016 forbids a business value in code and no source gives these lists, so they are held as data and parameters whose values are set at the baseline review; this keeps the story buildable without inventing an amount, a fee, a cut-off or a channel value.
read: FSD P6 v3 A2.16.3.1 (BR-P6-016, VR-P6-016-1, VR-P6-016-2); TSD P6 v2 T3.2; Business Rules and Routing Logic v4 R-RES-09 and R-SET-04; Template and Rules v1 R7.2 s17
confirm: The business analyst of P6 and the configuration owner confirm the parameter rows and the reference values before the wave starts, and the decision code and rule id are confirmed with the owner of the rule registry.
impact: A value change is a data change and not a release; a missing parameter row refuses both operations through the feature switch rather than guessing a list.

text: Both operations declare one capability area with right C on the POST and right R on the GET, scope applied, and the role lists stay in rwb-access; the customer path is authorised by ACE Common and gateway-bff against the case of the notice.
why: The matrix of TSD P6 T6.1 names no customer-facing right and the legacy permission checks carry the rights of the two notice operations and not of this act, so the area and the right are declared by the contract baseline and marked as a decision.
read: TSD P6 v2 T6.1 and T6.2; FSD P6 v3 A2.16.3.3; legacy RWB-E4-037 Permission checks; Template and Rules v1 R5.4 and R7.2 s10
confirm: The solution architect and the platform route owner confirm the capability area, the right and the customer path at the baseline review, and rwb-access holds the role lists.
impact: A wrong area or right refuses every caller with 403 until rwb-access is corrected; no code change is needed for a role list change.

text: A reference is treated as paid only on the owner answer and never on a derived rule, because no catalogue event reports a completed payment; the message IDs, the texts and the statuses of the three unnamed refusals stay the placeholder until the message list is published.
why: The event catalogue of Architecture v5 slide 42 holds no completed-payment event and the legacy validation table gives no message for a notice outside the eligible states, for nothing to pay against, or for an owner that does not answer, so the story reads the state from the owner and never invents a text.
read: Architecture v5 slide 42 A2 event catalogue; TSD P6 v2 T5.3; legacy RWB-E4-037 Validation and messages; FSD P6 v3 A2.16.4.3
confirm: The owner of the message list confirms the three messages, and the rwb-payment owner confirms whether a completed-payment event is added to the catalogue.
impact: A paid state that only the owner can state keeps the two schemas honest; when the event is added it is a consumed row of this service and an additive change of the contract.

text: The two channel operations of this key are new operations of rwb-comms on base /api/recovery/comms/v1, GET /notices/{noticeId}/channel-view and POST /notices/{noticeId}/views, because no inventory row serves an offer view.
why: The eleven P6 inventory rows hold no offer view and the legacy story provides no operation of its own, so the feature cannot be built without a surface.
read: TSD P6 Communications v2 T-A.1; FSD P6 Communications v3 A2.14; legacy RWB-E4-035 endpoint block
confirm: The rwb-comms tech lead and the solution architect confirm the two paths when the rwb-comms OpenAPI document is baselined.
impact: The app story, the edge route and the two channel surfaces call the two paths; a later rename needs a major version.

text: The offer of the case and the customer, the verified contact point and the consent are read on the rwb-source-data and rwb-treatment contracts one hop with a 2 s budget, and are faked from the first run because no P1 and no S2 contract story is in the C list of this key.
why: The plan names no P1 and no S2 contract story, yet AC1 and both validation rules rest on the consent, the contact stop and the offer.
read: Ownership Map v1; DP-05; Template and Rules v1 R5.4
confirm: The P1 and S2 owners confirm the two reads and publish the data product code and the offer field names.
impact: The story is Day 1 against the fakes; when the C rows are added the adapter is bound to the published shapes and no business code changes.

text: NoticeDelivered is published on the first delivery of a notice, WIN or digital, and a later view of an already Delivered notice records the view and publishes nothing.
why: The measure of the feature counts notices with proof of delivery and catalogue row 15 is the only row that carries it, while no source states the trigger or a dedupe rule across the two paths.
read: Architecture v5 Text Extract v1 slides 17 and 42; TSD P6 Communications v2 T5.3; FSD P6 Communications v3 A2.14.1; RWB-P6-E1055-CON
confirm: The event owner and rwb-case confirm the once-per-notice rule when the Kafka Topic and Event Catalog is next versioned.
impact: rwb-case starts its notice period once; a second event per notice would restart the period and confuse rwb-litigation and rwb-guarantee.

text: The view is a new table notice_view in rwb_comms with id, notice_id, case_id, channel, viewed_at and session_ref, and a view moves notice.delivery_status to DELIVERED and notice.callback_date to the view date.
why: No field of the notice carries the channel or the fact of a view, and the proof of delivery the measure counts has to be dated and countable.
read: TSD P6 Communications v2 T3.1 notice row; TSD P6 Communications v2 T3.2 LOV-DELIVERY; legacy RWB-E4-035 data table
confirm: The data steward and the P6 tech lead confirm the table and its columns when the Physical Schema is next versioned.
impact: One migration in rwb_comms and no change to the notice row beyond two nullable columns; a later rename of the table is a migration, not a contract change.

text: The two operations carry the capability area and the right of the notice resource they extend, Litigation R on the read and Litigation C on the write, the customer identity is authorised at the gateway-bff route, and the web channel of HOME.SCB is PORTAL.
why: TSD P6 T6.1 holds no customer role and no offer-view right, and LOV-CHANNEL holds no WEB value.
read: TSD P6 Communications v2 T6.1 and T3.2; T-A.1 API-P6-001 and API-P6-002; FSD P6 Communications v3 A2.14.3.3
confirm: The access architect and the P4 rwb-access owner confirm the right and the customer identity at the edge review.
impact: A customer role or a channel service identity added to rwb-access at the next version changes the enforcement point and not the operation; a WEB value would be a new LOV row.

text: The feature has no screen of its own: the two channel surfaces are LINE OA and HOME.SCB, reached through the gateway-bff composite route, and SCR-33 Template approval stays with the template stories.
why: The legacy screen shows a template, FSD P6 gives the feature no screen identifier, and the two channels are external.
read: FSD P6 Communications v3 A2.14.2 and A2.14.3.3; legacy RWB-E4-035 screen table; DP-19
confirm: The edge owner and the P6 business analyst confirm the surface list and the screen identifier at the next FSD version.
impact: No screen work in this key; the edge route and the two channel owners carry the presentation and the masking.
